title: Rangers sign Oliver Bjorkstrand to 1-year deal: How the free-agent winger fits in New York
content:
The New York Rangers have checked their right-winger box by signing Oliver Bjorkstrand to a one-year contract, a league source told The Athletic.

According to the source, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because the deal hasn’t been finalized, Bjorkstrand will carry a $4.5 million cap hit.

The 6-foot, 175-pounder from Denmark registered a 50.42 percent expected goals rate last season while ranking in the 64th percentile for speed bursts between 20 and 22 mph, according to NHL Edge. He gives New York a middle-six option who could slot in as a second-line winger if Vincent Trocheck is traded and captain J.T. Miller makes a permanent move to center. He also adds a right-handed shooter to a forward group that’s heavy on lefties.

The 31-year-old is coming off a few down seasons, including only 32 points (12 goals and 20 assists) in 80 games for the Tampa Bay Lightning last season, but he’s had as many as 59 points with the Seattle Kraken in 2023-24 and has posted six seasons of 20 goals or more.

A native of Denmark, Bjorkstrand was drafted by the Columbus Blue Jackets in the third round in 2013, spending the first five full NHL seasons of his career with the organization. According to PuckPedia, his deal with the Rangers includes no trade protection.

A top six featuring Bjorkstrand, Miller, Alexis Lafrenière, Gabe Perreault, Mika Zibanejad and newly acquired sniper Pavel Dorofeyev is a realistic starting point for the 2026-27 Rangers. That would allow 24-year-old winger Will Cuylle to slide into a more comfortable third-line role. And if another top-six option is acquired who bumps Bjorkstrand down (perhaps in a Trocheck trade), he also has experience playing lower in the lineup, which he primarily did with the Lightning.

He isn’t a game-changer or play-driver, but Bjorkstrand represents a low-risk bet who won’t hinder New York’s long-term flexibility. The deal leaves roughly $8.7 million in remaining cap space.

The length of the deal, which was first reported by Sportsnet, is also notable. The Rangers have added a little offense to their lineup in the short term to help them hang around in the playoff race. But if they fade from contention, Bjorkstrand can be used as a trade chip to recoup assets at the 2027 deadline.
